ask: Make every switch say "No internet: turn on mobile data or Wi-Fi", and let your PIN end the child's turn even offline (so you're never stuck). Gemini builds, Claude reviews, no new build needed. OK?
details:
**What happened (demo to a parent):** the internet was off, so "Play as" failed with a confusing message.

**Why it needs internet:** "Play as" really switches who is signed in, so the stars go to the child, not to you. Only our server can do that switch, and it checks your PIN there so a child can't find it on the phone. The lock itself (Android pinning) works offline.

**A bigger gap found while checking:** going back to you also needs the internet. If the internet drops during the child's turn, the "Time's up" screen can't be closed until it comes back (the phone's own PIN still unpins it, but the app stays paused).

**The fix (Gemini, small, update over the air):**
1. One clear message for every server action when offline: "No internet. Turn on mobile data or Wi-Fi, then try again." Checked *before* the phone is pinned. Also covers adding a child, link codes, class codes, feedback.
2. Your PIN also works offline: the phone keeps a scrambled copy of your PIN (set when you start Play as). Offline, the right PIN ends the turn (unpins, stops the timer, closes Time's up) and the app switches back to you as soon as the internet returns.

**Later, with the next app build:** a small "You're offline" strip at the top of the app (needs a new library, so not over the air).

**YES** = Claude writes the task, Gemini builds, Claude reviews before you see it.

title: Progress tabs reload everything on every switch (your note)
ask: Switching My children ↔ My classes reads every child's progress again (a teacher with 33 kids ≈ 100 reads per switch). My pick: A. YES = A. MORE DETAILS for B and C.
details:
**Cause (checked in code):** each tab is thrown away when you leave it and loads again from scratch when you come back.

**A. Keep what was loaded (recommended).** Tabs remember their data while the app is open; switching is instant and costs nothing. Fresh data: pull down to refresh, and it refreshes by itself if older than 10 minutes. Small app change, no server work.

**B. Live updates (what you suggested: pull only when something changes).** My pushback: a live connection on every child re-reads a child each time they answer, so during practice time a teacher's phone would read MORE, not less, and keep connections open. Good for 1–4 children, bad for a class of 33.

**C. One summary per class, kept by the server.** The teacher reads 1 document instead of 33+. Cheapest at scale (schools), but needs a server function and a deploy. Worth it before more schools join, not for the pilot.

My recommendation: A now, C before more schools.
note: Why do we need to refresh data for 10 minutes only. Why a teacher needs realtime data. What if we refresh dashboard hourly or say twice a day only. We need to understand who need to see what and who is the premium user to get instant updates

title: Help buttons: "Put in a class" goes to the teacher's waiting list?
ask: On People, "Put in a class" sends the person to that teacher's waiting list, not straight into the class, so the teacher still checks every child. YES (recommended) / NO = straight in.
details:
Why waiting list: the invite message promises families that the teacher checks every child. Straight in is faster, but a wrong child could land in a class with nobody checking.

The person sees on Home: "Waiting for Seema to approve 10-A". Every change is saved (who, when, before → after) with an Undo.

Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/Q7mpcL2kLC5oqr6LufFPi9 (section "Added 13 Nov").

title: Help buttons: "She's a parent" only after she names her child?
ask: You add a child profile for a parent only after she has told you the child's first name and class (e.g. on WhatsApp), and she confirms it on her phone. YES (recommended) / NO.
details:
On 12 Nov you said no to a "She's a parent" button, because kid profiles replace it. This version keeps it safe: we never guess a child, and the parent sees on Me: "Riya was added by the Apprec8 team. Right? Yes / Change".

NO = drop this button; parents add their own child (Me → Add my child) and you send them the WhatsApp message instead.

Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/Q7mpcL2kLC5oqr6LufFPi9 (section "Added 13 Nov").

title: Build all three Help buttons together?
ask: She's a teacher · She's a parent · Put in a class, built together (about a day), then a phone walk before publish. YES (recommended) / NO = only "She's a teacher" first / LATER.
details:
You deploy one new server function (I give the command). One server call per tap, no extra reads on anyone's phone. Nothing deletes.

Meanwhile the WhatsApp and Email buttons on stuck people are built and waiting for a 10-minute phone check before publish.

title: "I'm the parent on this phone": move the child's progress to a child profile?
ask: When a parent claims a Gmail the kid used, the kid's stars, class and progress move into the kid's own child profile (recorded), and the Gmail becomes the parent's. YES (recommended) / NO = the kid keeps the Gmail; the parent uses another one.
details:
Steps: grown-up check (year of birth 18+) → progress moves (nothing lost) → parent agrees in the app → Seema sees "parent confirmed" → the kid plays via "Let Riya play on this phone".

NO is simpler to build, but many families have only one Google account on the phone.

Spec: https://claude.ai/artifact/Q7mpcL2kLC5oqr6LufFPi9 (section "Added 13 Nov: learning-only").
